title: Slack came from a video game that shut down
summary: Tiny Speck's browser game Glitch opened to the public in September 2011 and shut down in December 2012. The team's internal messaging tool became the basis of Slack, which had over 10 million daily active users by 2019.

beats.say: A video game shut down, and its chat tool became Slack.
Glitch was a browser game made by a small company, Tiny Speck.
It opened to the public in September twenty eleven.
The company had raised over fifteen million dollars before beta testing.
Its engineers had also built a real time messaging tool for the team.
beats.cap: A chat tool for the team

beats.say: The game shut down in December twenty twelve.
As the game closed, the team saw the tool's value outside the company.
That tool became the basis for Slack.
By twenty nineteen, Slack had over ten million daily active users.
A closed game left behind a tool people kept using.

claims.note: TechCrunch: Tiny Speck raised more than $15 million in venture capital before beta testing

facts.claim: Tiny Speck, led by Stewart Butterfield, made the browser game Glitch, released to the public in September 2011
facts.note: Wikipedia (Glitch): developer Tiny Speck, official launch September 27, 2011; TechCrunch: browser-based game, released to the public in September 2011

facts.claim: Glitch shut down in December 2012 (the shutdown was confirmed in November 2012)
facts.note: Wikipedia (Glitch): officially shut down on December 9, 2012; TechCrunch: shutdown confirmed in November 2012

facts.claim: The internal messaging tool built for the team became the basis of Slack
facts.note: TechCrunch: engineers built a real-time messaging tool for internal communication; when Glitch was shutting down the team saw its value outside the company and it became the basis for Slack; Wikipedia agrees

facts.claim: Slack had more than 10 million daily active users by 2019
facts.note: TechCrunch, May 30, 2019: more than 10 million daily active users across more than 600,000 organizations
